addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Data Layer Analysis for `github.com/usememos/memos`

This is a Go project (the "Memos" note-taking application). The data/persistence layer lives in the **`/bench/repo/store/`** package. Protobuf message types used as payloads or rich settings are defined in **`/bench/repo/proto/store/`** (source) and generated into **`/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/`**.

The `store` package follows a clean pattern: each entity has a Go struct for the core row, plus companion structs for Find/Update/Delete operations, backed by a `Driver` interface (`/bench/repo/store/driver.go`) with implementations for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL under `/bench/repo/store/db/`.

---

| # | Entity Name | Primary Go Struct | Definition File | Database Table |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | **UserSetting** | `UserSetting` | `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` | `user_setting` |
| 3 | **UserIdentity** | `UserIdentity` | `/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go` | `user_identity` |
| 4 | **Memo** | `Memo` | `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` | `memo` |
| 5 | **MemoRelation** | `MemoRelation` | `/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go` | `memo_relation` |
| 6 | **MemoShare** | `MemoShare` | `/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go` | `memo_share` |
| 7 | **Attachment** | `Attachment` | `/bench/repo/store/attachment.go` | `attachment` |
| 8 | **IdentityProvider** | `IdentityProvider` | `/bench/repo/store/idp.go` | `idp` |
| 9 | **Inbox** | `Inbox` | `/bench/repo/store/inbox.go` | `inbox` |
| 10 | **Reaction** | `Reaction` | `/bench/repo/store/reaction.go` | `reaction` |
| 11 | **InstanceSetting** | `InstanceSetting` | `/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go` | `system_setting` |

---

### Detailed Breakdown per Entity

**1. User** (`/bench/repo/store/user.go`)
- Struct: `User` -- fields: `ID`, `RowStatus`, `CreatedTs`, `UpdatedTs`, `Username`, `Role`, `Email`, `Nickname`, `PasswordHash`, `AvatarURL`, `Description`
- Companion types: `UpdateUser`, `FindUser`, `DeleteUser`
- Custom type: `Role` (string enum: `ADMIN`, `USER`)

**2. UserSetting** (`/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go`)
- Struct: `UserSetting` -- fields: `UserID`, `Key` (protobuf enum), `Value` (JSON-encoded protobuf)
- Companion types: `FindUserSetting`, `DeleteUserSetting`, `RefreshTokenQueryResult`, `PATQueryResult`
- Values are protobuf messages: `ShortcutsUserSetting`, `GeneralUserSetting`, `TagsUserSetting`, `RefreshTokensUserSetting`, `PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting`, `WebhooksUserSetting`

**3. UserIdentity** (`/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go`)
- Struct: `UserIdentity` -- fields: `ID`, `UserID`, `Provider`, `ExternUID`, `CreatedTs`, `UpdatedTs`
- Companion types: `FindUserIdentity`, `DeleteUserIdentity`

**4. Memo** (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go`)
- Struct: `Memo` -- fields: `ID`, `UID`, `RowStatus`, `CreatorID`, `CreatedTs`, `UpdatedTs`, `Content`, `Visibility`, `Pinned`, `Payload` (protobuf `MemoPayload`), `ParentUID`
- Companion types: `FindMemo`, `FindMemoPayload`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`
- Custom type: `Visibility` (string enum: `PUBLIC`, `PROTECTED`, `PRIVATE`)

**5. MemoRelation** (`/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go`)
- Struct: `MemoRelation` -- fields: `MemoID`, `RelatedMemoID`, `Type`
- Companion types: `FindMemoRelation`, `DeleteMemoRelation`
- Custom type: `MemoRelationType` (string enum: `REFERENCE`, `COMMENT`)

**6. MemoShare** (`/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go`)
- Struct: `MemoShare` -- fields: `ID`, `UID`, `MemoID`, `CreatorID`, `CreatedTs`, `ExpiresTs`
- Companion types: `FindMemoShare`, `DeleteMemoShare`

**7. Attachment** (`/bench/repo/store/attachment.go`)
- Struct: `Attachment` -- fields: `ID`, `UID`, `CreatorID`, `CreatedTs`, `UpdatedTs`, `Filename`, `Blob`, `Type`, `Size`, `StorageType` (protobuf enum), `Reference`, `Payload` (protobuf `AttachmentPayload`), `MemoID`, `MemoUID`
- Companion types: `FindAttachment`, `UpdateAttachment`, `DeleteAttachment`

**8. IdentityProvider** (`/bench/repo/store/idp.go`)
- Struct: `IdentityProvider` -- fields: `ID`, `UID`, `Name`, `Type` (protobuf enum), `IdentifierFilter`, `Config` (JSON)
- Companion types: `FindIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProvider`, `DeleteIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProviderV1`

**9. Inbox** (`/bench/repo/store/inbox.go`)
- Struct: `Inbox` -- fields: `ID`, `CreatedTs`, `SenderID`, `ReceiverID`, `Status`, `Message` (protobuf `InboxMessage`)
- Companion types: `UpdateInbox`, `FindInbox`, `DeleteInbox`
- Custom type: `InboxStatus` (string enum: `UNREAD`, `ARCHIVED`)

**10. Reaction** (`/bench/repo/store/reaction.go`)
- Struct: `Reaction` -- fields: `ID`, `CreatedTs`, `CreatorID`, `ContentID`, `ReactionType`
- Companion types: `FindReaction`, `DeleteReaction`

**11. InstanceSetting** (`/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go`)
- Struct: `InstanceSetting` -- fields: `Name`, `Value`, `Description`
- Companion types: `FindInstanceSetting`, `DeleteInstanceSetting`
- Rich protobuf value types: `InstanceBasicSetting`, `InstanceGeneralSetting`, `InstanceStorageSetting`, `InstanceMemoRelatedSetting`, `InstanceTagsSetting`, `InstanceNotificationSetting`, `InstanceAISetting`

### Supporting Types (non-entity, shared)

- **`RowStatus`** (`/bench/repo/store/common.go`) -- string enum (`NORMAL`, `ARCHIVED`) used by `User` and `Memo`
- **`DeleteUserResult`** (`/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go`) -- result struct for cascading user deletion, contains collected `Attachments` and `UserSettingKeys`
- **`AuthenticationConfigState`** and **`AuthenticationConfigMutation`** (`/bench/repo/store/auth_config.go`) -- transactional validation types for authentication configuration changes (not standalone persisted entities)
- **`deploymentConfiguration`** (`/bench/repo/store/store.go`) -- in-memory runtime config aggregating file-backed identity providers and instance settings

---

### Protobuf-Defined Store Types

Source `.proto` files in `/bench/repo/proto/store/`:
- `attachment.proto` -- defines `AttachmentStorageType`, `AttachmentPayload`, `S3ObjectPayload`
- `idp.proto` -- defines `IdentityProvider`, `IdentityProvider_Type`, `IdentityProviderConfig`, `OAuth2Config`, `FieldMapping`
- `inbox.proto` -- defines `InboxMessage`, `InboxMessage_Type`
- `instance_setting.proto` -- defines `InstanceSetting`, `InstanceSettingKey`, and all the sub-setting messages
- `memo.proto` -- defines `MemoPayload` and related nested types
- `user_setting.proto` -- defines `UserSetting`, `UserSetting_Key`, and all per-key value messages

Generated Go code in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/`:
- `attachment.pb.go`
- `idp.pb.go`
- `inbox.pb.go`
- `instance_setting.pb.go`
- `memo.pb.go`
- `user_setting.pb.go`

---

### Database Driver Implementations

Each entity has a corresponding implementation file in all three database backends:
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/` (e.g., `user.go`, `memo.go`, `attachment.go`, etc.)
- `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/` (same file names)
- `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/` (same file names)

The canonical schema is visible in `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (and equivalents for postgres/mysql), which confirms all 11 tables listed above.

The data layer is the `store/` package (`store/*.go`), which defines 11 persistent entity types: User, Memo, Attachment, MemoRelation, MemoShare, Inbox, Reaction, IdentityProvider, UserSetting, UserIdentity, and InstanceSetting.

**2nd: User** — referenced from **7 packages** outside the store layer: `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`

These two are effectively tied at ~7 packages each. Memo edges out slightly when counting companion types like `Visibility` and `FindMemoPayload` which pull in additional runner packages, while User's reach is broader across auth-related packages. The next closest is **Attachment** at ~5 packages.
